Description:
Agreement template renders all five sections in order.
- Open the Agreement preview on the patient payment plan setup screen.
- Confirm the sections present.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a saved recurring payment plan Plan1; Plan1 = plan with a saved card Card1 and a complete Due On schedule; Client setting "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes (mandatory or non-mandatory) so the Agreement is available; Tpl1 = the default Payment Plan Agreement letter template applied to the database.
Test Data: A payment plan with card + schedule details.
Expected Output: The Agreement shows: Payment Details, Terms & Conditions, Cancellation Policy, Electronic Communications Consent, and Execution & Authorization (with the "Agree & Continue" checkbox), in that order.
Verification Step: 1. Log in and open Pat1 > Payment Plan and open Plan1 in the patient payment plan setup screen. 2. Click the Agreement button / save the plan so the Agreement preview opens. 3. Read the section headings from top to bottom and assert they appear in this order: Payment Details, Terms & Conditions, Cancellation Policy, Electronic Communications Consent, Execution & Authorization. 4. Assert none of the five sections is missing, duplicated or out of order. 5. Assert the Execution & Authorization section contains the "Agree & Continue" checkbox/button. 6. Scroll to the very bottom and confirm no unexpected extra section is rendered after Execution & Authorization. 7. Close and re-open the Agreement for Plan1 and confirm the same five sections render in the same order.

Description:
Agreement Payment Details merge fields populate from the plan.
- Open the Agreement preview for a plan with a saved card and an end date.
- Check each Payment Details line.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1 and mobile number Phone1 on the demographics screen; Plan1 = saved payment plan for Pat1 with recurring amount Amt1, frequency Freq1, an End Date End1 and a saved card Card1; Card1 = card with a brand, a last-4 and an expiry month/year; Total1 = the total authorized amount of Plan1.
Test Data: Amount, Frequency, card Brand+last 4+expiry, email/phone, Total Authorized, End Date all present.
Expected Output: Payment Details shows the real values: Payment Amount, Payment Frequency, Payment Method (Brand ending in <last 4> | Exp <date>), Patient Email/Text, Total Authorized Amount, and End Date — each filled from the plan, no leftover <placeholders>.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan, open Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. In the Payment Details section, assert Payment Amount equals Amt1 as saved on Plan1. 3. Assert Payment Frequency equals Freq1 exactly as configured in the Due On section. 4. Assert Payment Method shows Card1 brand + "ending in" its last 4 digits + its expiry, and that the full card number is never shown. 5. Assert Patient Email/Text show Email1 and Phone1 from Pat1 demographics. 6. Assert Total Authorized Amount equals Total1 and End Date equals End1. 7. Scan the whole Payment Details block and assert no un-merged placeholder token (any text still wrapped in angle brackets or braces) is left on screen.

Description:
Agreement notes that if the remaining balance is less than the payment amount, the final payment is only the remaining balance.
- Read the Payment Amount line in the Agreement.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1; Plan1 = plan with "Deduct amount only if patient has balance" ticked, recurring amount Amt1; Agreement available for Plan1 per the client setting.
Test Data: Any plan.
Expected Output: The Agreement states that if the remaining balance is less than the recurring amount, the final payment will be for the remaining balance only — matching the deduct-if-balance last-installment rule (RPP-PLAN-024).
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. Locate the Payment Amount line inside Payment Details. 3. Assert the wording states that if the remaining balance is less than the recurring amount, the final payment will be for the remaining balance only. 4. Assert this clause is present even when Plan1 has no End Date. 5. Confirm the clause matches the deduct-if-balance last-installment behaviour described for the plan (no contradicting wording elsewhere in the Agreement). 6. Confirm the clause text is static template wording and is not replaced by a numeric value.

Description:
Agreement Terms: a separate manual payment does not stop, reduce, or delay the next scheduled auto payment.
- Read the Manual Payments clause under Terms & Conditions.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1; Agreement available for Plan1 per the client setting; Tpl1 = the default Payment Plan Agreement template applied to the database.
Test Data: Any plan.
Expected Output: The Manual Payments clause clearly states a separate manual payment will not automatically stop, reduce, or delay the next scheduled automatic payment.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. Scroll to the Terms & Conditions section. 3. Locate the Manual Payments clause. 4. Assert it states that a separate manual payment will NOT automatically stop, reduce or delay the next scheduled automatic payment. 5. Assert the clause is present in the default template for every plan (re-check on a second plan Plan2 of another patient Pat2). 6. Confirm the clause is readable in the printed/PDF copy of the Agreement as well.

Description:
Agreement Terms: failed payments may be re-attempted within 30 calendar days, possibly with a returned-payment fee. 
- Read the Failed Payments clause.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1 using card Card1; Agreement available for Plan1; Tpl1 = default Payment Plan Agreement template.
Test Data: Any plan.
Expected Output: The Failed Payments clause states a declined charge may be re-attempted within 30 calendar days and a returned payment fee may be added to the second attempt, as permitted by the plan terms.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. Scroll to Terms & Conditions and find the Failed Payments clause. 3. Assert the clause states a declined charge may be re-attempted within 30 calendar days. 4. Assert the clause states a returned-payment fee may be added to the second attempt as permitted by the plan terms. 5. Assert the 30-day wording is fixed template text and does not change with the plan frequency. 6. Confirm the same clause appears on the Agreement of a second plan Plan2 to prove it comes from the default template.

Description:
Agreement Cancellation Policy requires at least 3 business days' notice before the payment date.
- Read the Cancellation Policy.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1 that has an End Date End1; Agreement available for Plan1; Tpl1 = default Payment Plan Agreement template.
Test Data: Any plan.
Expected Output: The Cancellation Policy states the authorization remains until the total is paid, the end date is reached, or the patient cancels, and that at least 3 business days' notice before the payment date is required to avoid the next charge.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. Scroll to the Cancellation Policy section. 3. Assert it states the authorization stays in force until the total is paid, the end date is reached, or the patient cancels. 4. Assert it states at least 3 business days notice before the payment date is required to avoid the next charge. 5. Assert the notice period reads "business days" (not calendar days). 6. Re-open the Agreement on a plan without an end date and confirm the Cancellation Policy wording is still present.

Description:
Agreement "Agree & Continue" is the execution/authorization step that activates the plan.
- Read the Execution & Authorization section.
- Tick "Agree & Continue".
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a newly saved payment plan Plan1 awaiting agreement; client setting "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes & keep it mandatory; Agreement window opens after Save.
Test Data: A plan awaiting agreement.
Expected Output: Ticking "Agree & Continue" records the patient's authorization to the automatic payment terms and electronic communications consent, and (per the client setting) activates the plan.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan, create/save Plan1 so the Agreement window opens. 2. Scroll to the Execution & Authorization section and read the authorization wording. 3. Tick / click "Agree & Continue". 4. Assert the system records the patient authorization (the Agreement now shows as agreed with date/time stamp or signature). 5. Re-open Plan1 and assert its status is Active because the agreement was accepted. 6. Assert the electronic communications consent is recorded together with the authorization. 7. Negative check: repeat on a second plan Plan2, close the window without agreeing, and confirm the plan is saved but left Inactive.
Status Comment:
"Description: replace with:
""Agreement 'Agree & Continue' records authorization; for a mandatory agreement it is required before the saved plan can become Active.""

Expected Output: replace with:
""Agree & Continue records authorization. When client setting = Yes & Keep it mandatory, closing without agreement leaves the saved plan Inactive; agreeing allows it to become Active.""

Verification Step: replace with:
""1. Set Show Agreement on Payment Plan = Yes & Keep it mandatory. 2. Save a new plan. 3. Close Agreement without agreeing and assert plan is saved Inactive. 4. Reopen Agreement and click Agree & Continue. 5. Assert authorization is recorded and plan becomes Active.""
"

Description:
Payment Plan Setup letter (Email + Text) populates correctly; the outstanding-balance line shows only when an end date exists.
- Trigger the Payment Plan Setup notification for a plan WITH an end date, then for one WITHOUT.
- Check both the Email and Text versions.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1 and mobile Phone1; Plan1 = saved payment plan for Pat1 WITH an End Date; Plan2 = saved payment plan (same or another patient) WITHOUT an End Date; Notification preference for the Payment Plan Setup event is enabled for both Email and Text; Tpl1 = default Payment Plan Setup letter template.
Test Data: One plan with an end date; one without.
Expected Output: The Email shows recurring amount, frequency, first payment date and payment method; the Text is the short version. The "Total Outstanding Balance" line appears only when the plan has an end date, and is omitted otherwise.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Plan Setup notification (Email + Text) in the notification preference for the Payment Plan event type. 2. Save Plan1 so the setup notification is triggered, then open the generated Email in the notification/communication log. 3. Assert the Email shows the recurring amount, the frequency, the first payment date and the payment method of Plan1. 4. Assert the Email for Plan1 contains the Total Outstanding Balance line. 5. Open the Text version for Plan1 and assert it carries the same key facts in short form. 6. Repeat for Plan2 (no End Date) and assert the Total Outstanding Balance line is NOT present in either the Email or the Text. 7. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain in either letter.

Description:
Payment Plan Status Update letter (Email + Text) shows previous status, new status and effective date; balance line only with an end date.
- Trigger the Status Update notification after a status change.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 that has an End Date; Plan2 = payment plan without an End Date; Status1 = the status of the plan before the change; Status2 = the status after the change; Notification preference for the Payment Plan Status Change event enabled for Email and Text.
Test Data: A plan whose status changed.
Expected Output: The letter shows Previous Status, New Status and Effective Date, plus a Remaining Balance line only when an end date exists. The Text version carries the short "status changed to <status> on <date>" message.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Plan Status Change notification (Email + Text). 2. Change Plan1 status from Status1 to Status2 and save. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert it shows Previous Status = Status1, New Status = Status2 and an Effective Date equal to the date the change was made. 5. Assert the Remaining Balance line is present because Plan1 has an End Date. 6. Open the Text version and assert it carries the short "status changed to <new status> on <date>" message with the same values. 7. Repeat the status change on Plan2 and assert the Remaining Balance line is omitted. 8. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain.

Description:
Payment Successful letter (Email + Text) shows amount, date, method, confirmation number; plan balance only with an end date.
- Trigger the Payment Successful notification after a successful charge.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 (End Date set) and saved card Card1; Plan2 = plan without an End Date; Amt1 = the installment amount charged; Notification preference for the Payment Successful event enabled for Email and Text; a successful charge exists on Plan1.
Test Data: A successful plan charge.
Expected Output: The letter shows Amount Paid, Date Processed, Payment Method (brand + last 4 + expiry), Confirmation Number, and a Remaining Plan Balance line only when an end date exists.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Successful notification (Email + Text). 2. Run or trigger a successful charge on Plan1 (scheduled run or Pay Now). 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert Amount Paid equals the amount actually charged, and Date Processed equals the date of the successful transaction. 5. Assert Payment Method shows Card1 brand + last 4 + expiry only (never the full card number). 6. Assert a Confirmation Number is present and not blank. 7. Assert the Remaining Plan Balance line is shown for Plan1 (End Date exists) and is omitted after a successful charge on Plan2. 8. Open the Text version and assert it repeats amount and date consistently.

Description:
Payment Failed letter (Email + Text) states the failed amount/date, the retry timing, and next steps.
- Trigger the Payment Failed notification after a declined charge.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and a card Card1 that will be declined by the gateway; Notification preference for the Payment Failed event enabled for Email and Text; Retry1 = the configured retry interval.
Test Data: A failed plan charge.
Expected Output: The letter states the payment could not be processed, that it will be retried after the configured time, and next steps (call the clinic to update details). The Text version is the short "Payment of $ on <date> failed" message.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Failed notification (Email + Text). 2. Force a scheduled charge on Plan1 to be declined by the gateway. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert it states the payment could not be processed and shows the failed amount and the failed date. 5. Assert it states the payment will be retried after the configured retry time Retry1. 6. Assert it gives next steps (contact the clinic to update payment details). 7. Open the Text version and assert it carries the short failed-payment message with the same amount and date. 8. Assert the letter does not expose full card details.

Description:
Card Expiring reminder (Email + Text) shows the card last 4 and treats the expiry as the last day of the expiring month.
- Trigger the Card Expiring reminder for a card whose month is ending.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 using card Card1; Card1 = saved card whose expiry month/year is the month about to end; Notification preference for the Card Expiry reminder enabled for Email and Text; the Card Expiry reminder schedule is due to run.
Test Data: A card nearing expiry.
Expected Output: The reminder shows the card ending in <last 4> and states it expires on the last day of the expiring month, prompting the patient to update the card to avoid a payment failure.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Card Expiry reminder (Email + Text) in the notification/reminder preference. 2. Let the Card Expiry reminder run for Plan1 / Card1. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert it identifies the card as "ending in" the last 4 digits of Card1 and never shows the full number. 5. Assert the expiry date printed in the letter is the LAST day of Card1 expiry month (not the first day and not the raw month/year only). 6. Assert the letter prompts the patient to update the card to avoid a payment failure. 7. Open the Text version and assert the same last-4 and the same expiry date are used. 8. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain.

Description:
Payment Due reminder (Email + Text) shows the scheduled amount, processing date, method, and "in X days".
- Trigger the Payment Due reminder ahead of a scheduled charge.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 with an upcoming scheduled charge on date Due1 and saved card Card1; Amt1 = the scheduled installment amount; Lead1 = the configured number of days before the due date at which the Payment Due reminder runs; notification preference for the Payment Due reminder enabled for Email and Text.
Test Data: An upcoming scheduled charge.
Expected Output: The reminder shows the Scheduled Amount, Processing Date, and the Payment Method on file, and states the auto-payment will be processed in X days with no action needed if details are up to date.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Due reminder (Email + Text) with lead time Lead1. 2. Let the reminder run Lead1 days before Due1 for Plan1. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert the Scheduled Amount equals Amt1 and the Processing Date equals Due1. 5. Assert the Payment Method on file shows Card1 brand + last 4 only. 6. Assert the letter states the auto-payment will be processed in the correct number of days and that no action is needed if details are up to date. 7. Open the Text version and assert amount and date match the Email. 8. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain.

Description:
Across all letters, balance/outstanding lines appear only when the plan has an end date, and the clinic email setup is the sender.
- Trigger any two payment-plan letters — one for a plan with an end date, one without.
- Check the balance lines and the email sender.
Pre-requisite Data: Plan1 = payment plan WITH an End Date; Plan2 = payment plan WITHOUT an End Date; Office1 = the clinic whose e-mail setup is configured with sender address Sender1; notification preferences for at least two payment-plan letter events enabled for Email.
Test Data: One plan with an end date; one without.
Expected Output: Any "Total Outstanding / Remaining Balance" line is shown only when the plan has an end date (omitted for open-ended plans). All payment-plan emails are sent from the clinic's configured email setup.
Verification Step: 1. Configure Office1 e-mail setup with sender address Sender1. 2. Trigger any payment-plan letter for Plan1 and open the generated Email. 3. Assert the "Total Outstanding / Remaining Balance" line is present because Plan1 has an End Date. 4. Trigger the same letter for Plan2 and assert the balance line is completely omitted (no empty label, no zero value). 5. Repeat steps 2-4 with a second payment-plan letter type to prove the rule is template-wide. 6. Inspect the From address of every generated Email and assert it equals Sender1 from the Office1 e-mail setup, not a user mailbox or a hard-coded system address. 7. Confirm the same sender is used for both the with-end-date and no-end-date letters.
Status Comment: Conditional balance + clinic-email sender across templates.

Description: [New] Confirmation Number in the Payment Successful letter is filled with the payment number generated for the credit-card transaction.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 paid by saved card Card1; PayNo1 = the payment number the system generates for a credit-card transaction of Plan1; notification preference for the Payment Successful event enabled for Email.
Test Data: Run one successful credit-card charge on Plan1; note PayNo1 from the transaction/receipt record.
Expected Output: The Confirmation Number merge field in the Payment Successful letter is populated with PayNo1 — the payment number generated for that credit-card transaction — and not with the plan number, the installment number or a blank value.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Successful notification (Email) for the Payment Plan event type. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and run a successful credit-card charge (scheduled run or Pay Now). 3. Open the created receipt / Transaction Tracking row for that charge and note the generated payment number PayNo1. 4. Open the Payment Successful Email produced for that charge from the notification log. 5. Assert the Confirmation Number field is not blank and its value is exactly PayNo1. 6. Assert the Confirmation Number is NOT the payment plan number, the installment number or the receipt sequence of some other transaction. 7. Run a second successful charge on Plan1 and assert the new letter carries the NEW payment number, proving the field is per-transaction.

Description: [New] Confirmation Number in the Payment Successful letter matches the payment number shown on Transaction Tracking for the same charge.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; PayNo1 = payment number of the credit-card transaction; Transaction Tracking screen accessible for Plan1.
Test Data: One successful credit-card charge on Plan1; compare the letter against the Transaction Tracking row.
Expected Output: The Confirmation Number printed in the letter is identical to the payment number displayed for the same transaction on the Transaction Tracking screen, so the patient can quote it to the clinic.
Verification Step: 1. Run a successful credit-card charge on Plan1. 2. Open Transaction Tracking filtered to Plan1 and locate the row for that charge. 3. Note the payment number PayNo1 on that row. 4. Open the Payment Successful Email for the same charge. 5. Assert the Confirmation Number equals PayNo1 character for character. 6. Assert the letter amount and date also match the same Transaction Tracking row. 7. Repeat for a second charge and confirm each letter maps to its own transaction row.

Description: [New] A Pay Now credit-card payment also produces a Payment Successful letter carrying that Pay Now transaction payment number.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a saved payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; PayNo1 = payment number generated for the Pay Now credit-card transaction; Payment Successful notification enabled for Email and Text.
Test Data: Use Pay Now on Plan1 with a credit-card payment method and let it succeed.
Expected Output: The Pay Now credit-card payment triggers the Payment Successful letter and its Confirmation Number is the payment number generated for that Pay Now transaction, not for a scheduled installment.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and click Pay Now. 2. Choose a payment option, pay with card Card1 and let the transaction succeed. 3. Note the payment number PayNo1 from the resulting receipt. 4. Open the Payment Successful Email generated for this Pay Now payment. 5. Assert the Confirmation Number equals PayNo1. 6. Assert the Amount Paid equals the amount actually collected through Pay Now. 7. Assert only ONE Payment Successful letter is generated for this single Pay Now transaction.

Description: [New] Card Expiry reminder always prints the LAST day of the expiry month as the card expiry date.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; Card1 = card stored with an expiry month and year only (no day); Card Expiry reminder enabled for Email and Text in the reminder preference.
Test Data: Card1 saved with an expiry month/year; let the Card Expiry reminder run for Plan1.
Expected Output: Because only month and year are captured for a card, the reminder treats the expiry date as the LAST calendar day of that month and prints that full date in both the Email and the Text version.
Verification Step: 1. Save card Card1 on Plan1 with an expiry month/year. 2. Enable the Card Expiry reminder (Email + Text) for the Payment Plan event type. 3. Let the reminder run for Plan1. 4. Open the generated Email and read the expiry date printed for Card1. 5. Assert the date is the last calendar day of Card1 expiry month in Card1 expiry year. 6. Assert it is not the first day of the month and not a bare month/year string. 7. Open the Text version and assert the identical date is used. 8. Assert the card is identified only by its last 4 digits.

Description: [New] Card Expiry reminder last-day rule is correct for 31-day, 30-day, 28-day and leap-year February expiry months.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1..Pat4 = patients each with a payment plan and a saved card CardA/CardB/CardC/CardD; CardA expires in a 31-day month, CardB in a 30-day month, CardC in a non-leap February, CardD in a leap-year February; Card Expiry reminder enabled.
Test Data: Four cards whose expiry months have 31, 30, 28 and 29 days respectively.
Expected Output: For every card the reminder prints the correct last day of that month: the 31st for a 31-day month, the 30th for a 30-day month, the 28th for a non-leap February and the 29th for a leap-year February.
Verification Step: 1. Set up one plan per card CardA, CardB, CardC and CardD with the expiry months described in the pre-requisite data. 2. Enable the Card Expiry reminder and let it run for all four plans. 3. Open the reminder for CardA and assert the expiry date is the 31st of its month. 4. Open the reminder for CardB and assert the expiry date is the 30th of its month. 5. Open the reminder for CardC and assert the expiry date is the 28th of February. 6. Open the reminder for CardD and assert the expiry date is the 29th of February. 7. Assert no reminder rolls over into the following month. 8. Assert Email and Text versions agree for each card.

Description: [New] A card is not treated as expired before the last day of its expiry month, so scheduled charges before that day still run.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; Card1 expiry month is the current month; Due1 = a scheduled installment date that falls earlier in the same month than the last day.
Test Data: Plan1 with a charge scheduled on Due1, which is before the last day of Card1 expiry month.
Expected Output: The charge on Due1 is attempted normally because Card1 is considered valid until the last day of its expiry month; the card is only treated as expired after that last day.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 with card Card1 whose expiry month is the current month. 2. Confirm an installment is scheduled on Due1, earlier in the month than its last day. 3. Let the scheduled run execute on Due1. 4. Assert the charge is attempted and not blocked with an expired-card error. 5. Assert the installment status reflects the gateway outcome and is not forced to Overdue purely because of expiry. 6. Assert the Card Expiry reminder for Card1 still quotes the last day of the month as the expiry date. 7. Negative check: confirm no expired-card message is shown for Card1 before that last day.

Description: [New] Every payment-plan notification and reminder e-mail is sent from the clinic e-mail setup address.
Pre-requisite Data: Office1 = clinic with an e-mail setup configured with sender address Sender1; Pat1 = patient of Office1 with payment plan Plan1; notification/reminder preferences enabled for Email for the Payment Plan events (setup, status change, successful, failed, payment due, card expiry).
Test Data: Trigger each payment-plan Email event for Plan1 at Office1.
Expected Output: The From address of every payment-plan notification and reminder Email is Sender1, taken from the clinic e-mail setup — not the logged-in user mailbox and not a hard-coded application address.
Verification Step: 1. Configure Office1 e-mail setup with sender address Sender1. 2. Enable the Email channel for all payment-plan notification and reminder events. 3. Trigger the Payment Plan Setup event by saving Plan1 and open the generated Email. 4. Assert the From/sender address is Sender1. 5. Repeat for the Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Due and Card Expiry events. 6. Assert every one of those Emails uses Sender1 as the sender. 7. Negative check: assert none of them is sent from the logged-in user personal mailbox or from a default system address.

Description: [New] Changing the clinic e-mail setup changes the sender of subsequently generated payment-plan e-mails.
Pre-requisite Data: Office1 = clinic with e-mail setup sender Sender1; Sender2 = a different valid sender address; Pat1 = patient of Office1 with payment plan Plan1; at least one payment-plan Email event enabled.
Test Data: Send one payment-plan Email with Sender1, change the clinic e-mail setup to Sender2, then send the same event again.
Expected Output: E-mails generated after the change go out from Sender2; already-sent e-mails keep the sender they were sent with, proving the sender is read from the clinic e-mail setup at send time.
Verification Step: 1. With Office1 e-mail setup = Sender1, trigger a payment-plan Email for Plan1 and note the sender. 2. Assert the sender is Sender1. 3. Change the Office1 e-mail setup sender to Sender2 and save. 4. Trigger the same payment-plan Email event again for Plan1. 5. Assert the new Email is sent from Sender2. 6. Re-open the first Email in the log and assert its recorded sender is still Sender1. 7. Assert no error or blank sender occurs during the change.

Description: [New] Payment-plan e-mails use the e-mail setup of the clinic the plan belongs to when more than one clinic is configured.
Pre-requisite Data: Office1 and Office2 = two clinics with different e-mail setups Sender1 and Sender2; Plan1 = payment plan belonging to Office1; Plan2 = payment plan belonging to Office2; payment-plan Email events enabled for both.
Test Data: Trigger the same payment-plan Email event once for Plan1 and once for Plan2.
Expected Output: The e-mail for Plan1 is sent from Office1 e-mail setup (Sender1) and the e-mail for Plan2 from Office2 e-mail setup (Sender2); the clinic of the plan decides the sender.
Verification Step: 1. Configure different sender addresses Sender1 for Office1 and Sender2 for Office2. 2. Trigger a payment-plan Email event for Plan1 (Office1). 3. Assert the sender is Sender1. 4. Trigger the same event for Plan2 (Office2). 5. Assert the sender is Sender2. 6. Assert the sender does not change when the same user, logged in once, triggers both. 7. Negative check: assert Plan2 e-mail is never sent from Sender1.

Description: [New] A default letter template exists for each of the seven payment-plan events: Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry and Payment Plan Agreement.
Pre-requisite Data: A database where the payment-plan default letter templates have been applied; the letter/template setup screen is accessible; Ev1..Ev7 = the seven payment-plan events listed in the description.
Test Data: Open the letter template setup and list the payment-plan templates.
Expected Output: All seven payment-plan default templates are present and usable: Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry and the Payment Plan Agreement.
Verification Step: 1. Open the letter/template setup screen and filter to payment-plan templates. 2. Assert a default template exists for Payment Successful. 3. Assert a default template exists for Payment Failed. 4. Assert default templates exist for Payment Plan Setup and Payment Plan Status Change. 5. Assert default templates exist for the Payment Due and Card Expiry reminders. 6. Assert a default Payment Plan Agreement template exists. 7. Assert each of the seven opens without error and has non-empty body content. 8. Negative check: assert none of the seven is missing or shows a blank/placeholder-only body.

Description: [New] The seven payment-plan default templates are applied to all databases by default, without any manual setup.
Pre-requisite Data: DB1 = a database where no one has manually created payment-plan templates; Pat1 = patient in DB1 with payment plan Plan1; notification/reminder preferences for payment-plan events can be enabled in DB1.
Test Data: A fresh database DB1 with no manually created payment-plan letter templates.
Expected Output: Without any manual template creation, all seven payment-plan default templates are already available in DB1 and the notification/reminder events can be enabled and produce fully formatted letters.
Verification Step: 1. Log into DB1 where no payment-plan templates were manually created. 2. Open the letter template setup and assert the seven payment-plan default templates are already present. 3. Enable a payment-plan notification event and assert its default template is auto-selected / available for selection. 4. Trigger that event for Plan1 and open the generated letter. 5. Assert the letter renders with full default content and merged values, not an empty body. 6. Repeat for one reminder event (Payment Due or Card Expiry) and assert the same. 7. Assert the user was never asked to create a template manually.

Description: [New] Each payment-plan default template provides both the Email and the Text layout where the event supports both channels.
